transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

Don’t panic! A flashing U code on a Beko (and many other brands like Bosch, Siemens, or Whirlpool) induction hob almost never means the unit is faulty, especially if it’s brand new.

### What does "U" mean?
On most induction hobs, "U" stands for "Unknown Cookware" or "No Compatible Pan."

Induction hobs only work with magnetic cookware (ferrous metal). If the hob doesn’t detect a suitable pan on the zone, it will flash U and refuse to heat. This is a safety and efficiency feature.

---

### Why is this happening?
Even though your hob is new, here are the most common reasons for the "U" error:

#### 1. Your saucepan isn’t induction-compatible
• Not all pans work on induction. Only pans with a magnetic base will work.
• Test: Hold a magnet to the bottom of your pan. If it sticks firmly, it should work. If it doesn’t stick, it won’t work on induction.
• Common non-induction pans: Aluminum, copper, glass, ceramic (unless they have a special magnetic disk embedded in the base), and some stainless steel (if not magnetic).

#### 2. The pan is too small or has an uneven base
• Induction hobs require the pan’s base to be large enough to cover most of the heating zone (usually at least 12cm diameter, but check your manual).
• If the base is warped, ridged, or very thin, the hob may not detect it properly.

#### 3. The pan isn’t centered correctly
• Place the pan squarely in the middle of the cooking zone. Off-center placement can sometimes cause detection issues.

#### 4. There’s debris between the pan and the hob
• Check for any crumbs, liquid spills, or protective film residue on the glass surface where the pan sits. Clean it thoroughly with a damp cloth and dry it well.

#### 5. The hob is in "Demo" or "Store" mode (less likely but possible)
• Some new appliances come in a demo mode for shop displays. However, this usually shows different codes (like "F" or specific error patterns). Still, worth checking your manual.

---

### What to do now:
1. Try a different pan: Use a known induction-compatible pan (e.g., a standard stainless steel pot with a magnetic base). If it works, your original saucepan is the issue.
2. Check the magnet test on your current saucepan.
3. Clean the hob surface thoroughly and ensure it’s completely dry.
4. Re-center the pan on the zone.

---

### When to call for service:
If you try a known good induction pan, center it properly, clean the surface, and it still flashes "U" and doesn’t heat, then there may be an issue with the hob’s sensor or installation. In that case:
• Contact Beko customer support or the retailer where you bought it.
• Since it’s brand new, you’re covered under warranty, so don’t attempt to open it yourself.

Most likely scenario: Your saucepan just isn’t induction-compatible! Try a different pan first. 😊
Ok I tried the magnet thing - it doesn't stick to my saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole and that one heated fine. So is it just my pans?

Yes, exactly! Your diagnosis is spot on. 🎯

Since the magnet didn’t stick to your saucepan, that pan contains no ferrous metal (like iron or magnetic stainless steel). Induction hobs work by creating a magnetic field that heats only the cookware itself. If the pan isn't magnetic, the hob can't "grab" it to generate heat, so it flashes U (Unknown/No Cookware) as a safety measure.

### Why did your cast-iron casserole work?
Cast iron is highly magnetic, which is why the magnet stuck and the hob detected it perfectly. This confirms:
1.  ✅ Your new Beko induction hob is working correctly.
2.  ❌ Your saucepan is not compatible with induction cooking.

### What can you do about your non-induction pans?
You have a few options if you want to keep using those specific saucepans:

#### Option 1: Buy an "Induction Interface Disk" (Best for occasional use)
This is a flat, magnetic metal disk that sits on the hob. The hob heats the disk, and the disk transfers heat to your non-induction pan.
• Pros: Allows you to use aluminum, copper, or glass pans.
• Cons: It’s less efficient (slower heating), uses more energy, and can be tricky to clean around.

#### Option 2: Replace incompatible pans with induction-compatible ones (Best long-term solution)
Induction cooking is faster, safer, and more energy-efficient than gas or ceramic hobs. Many modern saucepans are designed specifically for it. Look for the induction symbol on the bottom of new pans (it looks like a coil/spiral).

#### Option 3: Check if your stainless steel pans might work
Some stainless steel pans are magnetic, but not all. Try the magnet test again on different parts of the base. If it sticks anywhere on the base, it should work. If it’s truly non-magnetic (like some high-end tri-ply pans without an iron core), they won’t work.

### Summary:
• Your hob is fine. It’s doing exactly what it’s supposed to do by refusing to heat a pan it can’t detect.
• Your saucepan is the issue. It’s not induction-compatible.
• Quick fix: Use an interface disk if you must use that specific pan, or invest in new induction-ready pans for the best experience.

Enjoy your new hob! Induction cooking is fantastic once you have the right pans. 😊
